item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J02665","case1_error":"Reports 200 pairs instead of converting to the requested 400 individual plugs.","case2_error":"Makes Richard 20 years younger, implying a current age of −6; he must be older, giving combined future ages of 128.","reason":"The first answers in the wrong unit; the second reverses the age relationship.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02666","case1_error":"Treats Frank's 12 sold apples as his remaining apples, instead of subtracting them from 36.","case2_error":"Counts only three diners, omitting Bret from Bret plus three coworkers.","reason":"The first confuses a removed portion with the remainder; the second omits a person from the total count.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02667","case1_error":"Uses doubled two-week vegetable consumption as weekly consumption before adding weekly kale.","case2_error":"Interprets three apples as per teacher rather than per child; the wording leaves this allocation materially ambiguous.","reason":"The first clearly mixes time periods, but the second depends on an ambiguous interpretation of the apple allocation.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J02668","case1_error":"Reverses Ida's more-than relationship, then replaces Ida's and Patty's calculated prices with unsupported values.","case2_error":"Invents Sam = Giselle − 15, applying Isabella's comparison with Giselle to the wrong person.","reason":"The first reverses a comparison and arbitrarily revises values; the second assigns a comparison to the wrong pair of people.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02669","case1_error":"Treats the calculated $150 earnings for all three men as earnings per man and multiplies by three again.","case2_error":"Treats the $2 price for five cans as a per-can price and multiplies by ten.","reason":"Both treat a group-level amount as a per-member amount, causing an extra multiplication by group size.","judgment":"same"}]}
